headline: Rare variants and functional annotations extend genotype-based trait prediction
label: Genomic Prediction And Polygenic Scores
summary: Published frameworks now add rare variants and functional annotations to common-variant risk models, improving prediction across populations and traits.
synthesis: The dominant thread is extending genotype-based prediction beyond standard common-variant models by integrating heterogeneous data layers. RICE combines common-variant ensemble learning with rare-variant gene-level testing and penalized regression, evaluated across diverse populations for polygenic risk prediction. IFAM extends linear mixed models with multiple random effects to integrate many functional annotation types, improving genomic prediction accuracy for complex traits. The type 1 diabetes study pairs genome-wide association and fine-mapping of 20,355 cases, yielding 160 risk signals, with a machine learning model, T1GRS, that improves risk prediction. The ECG foundation model represents a distinct data modality, yet it contributes to the same aim through prediction of eight cardiovascular diseases and genetic factor discovery. What is new relative to common-variant genomic prediction is explicit joint inclusion of rare variants and functional annotations within a single prediction framework.
